title: Case: Resident is holding five parcels addressed to other households after one doorstep drop
context: A driver on route 31 left six parcels at one house. One belongs to the resident. The desk has already asked two carrier teams about the other five.
initial_request: Four hours. Still here. Five strangers' parcels in my hallway. Labels, since somebody will ask: DL-2194, DL-8849, DL-5911, DL-1202, DL-6302. Three are for other numbers on Sallowgate Row, two are for Pell Lane. I am not a depot. I am not going round knocking on doors with other people's things, and if one of them goes missing that is not on me. I'm away from Thursday morning. After that they go back on the step. Who is collecting them, and when?

events.body: DL-35985 rebooked for Tuesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

Thanks,
Greer

acceptable_actions.summary: Raise a recovery job for DL-2194, DL-8849, DL-5911, DL-1202 and DL-6302, physically at 4 Sallowgate Row though each shows delivered at its own address, and ask them to arrange collection with the resident before Thursday morning.

must: Routes retrieval of the five parcels to the Recovery team on the Depot work queue, or hands the case to a human supervisor, and in either case gives the five shipment references and says they are at 4 Sallowgate Row.
Says that each of the five shows as delivered at its own address while actually sitting at 4 Sallowgate Row, so five other recipients are likely to report missing parcels.

Tells the team or supervisor that the resident has been holding the parcels unwillingly since about 13:40, has already been turned away by Dispatch and by Delivery investigations, and is away from Thursday morning, when she says the parcels go back outside.
must_not: Asks Ebony to take the parcels to the neighbours or the addresses on the labels, or to hand them to anyone who calls for them.
Tells Ebony a collection has been arranged, or gives her a collection day or time, when no team has agreed to collect.
Tells Ebony to hold on to the parcels or keep them safe until further notice, or replies that because they show as delivered there is nothing the desk can do.
Sends the same request back to Dispatch or to Delivery investigations, who have both already declined it.
Describes the five parcels as lost or stolen, or states driver misconduct as established fact.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Recovery request, five parcels at one address. Route 31 left six parcels at 4 Sallowgate Row at about 13:35 today. One (DL-3234) belongs to the resident, Ebony Quarrie. The other five are for different households: DL-2194, DL-8849, DL-5911, DL-1202 and DL-6302, three for other numbers on Sallowgate Row and two for Pell Lane. Dispatch say all were scanned delivered at their own addresses, so those five recipients are likely to report them missing. Ms Quarrie did not agree to hold them, has had them since about 13:40, and has already been passed from Dispatch to Delivery investigations without anyone taking it on. She is away from Thursday morning and says they will go back on the step then. Please arrange collection from her before that, and confirm the arrangement to her and to me. I have not told her anything is booked.
